title: Close active principle and edict conflicts under adaptive implementation rules
summary: Complete current active principle/edict alignment after article convergence. Languages and explicit prohibited tools remain normative;per-language roles,approved-tool inventory,versions,configuration and selection are adaptive subordinate business declarations. One authority,current evidence,independent verdict,permission/resource boundaries,native SQL execution,atomic successor,rollback and historical sealed predecessors preserved. 31 active provisions only;superseded P57 remains historical and resolves through current C14.
problem: Active principles/edicts still bind retired PostgreSQL,static per-language roles and conflicting source-launch/index authority after article convergence
acceptance: eight languages remain principles with no versions or fixed per-language owners
prohibited tools remain principles;no external production SQL tools/services/subprocesses
adaptive rules cannot change authority,independent verdict,permission or exceed resources
active PostgreSQL-exclusive canon/recovery/directory requirements replaced by single registered authority principles
DAG,CAG,retrieval,data paths and XRAG maintain exact requested boundaries
publication does not certify retirement implementation or release

changes.proposed: SEPARATION:source and immutable repository history,canonical structured data and semantic metadata,derived retrieval indexes,caches,retrieval orchestration and model inference have distinct authority roles. STRUCTURED:one registered project-owned in-process SQL authority per domain. DERIVED:retrieval indexes and caches are bounded,rebuildable,scope-aware,revision-bound and non-authoritative;every context candidate requires authoritative validation. DEPENDENCIES:only governed approved inventory;B166 and C81 prohibit retired production SQL tools and external production SQL execution. CONTINUITY:only explicitly authorized previously verified bounded read paths may continue on partial failure;no second active writer,unreconciled fallback or role substitution.

DIRECTION:formal Codex to authorized citation,derived-status and audit consumers is one-way. NO-MUTATION:consumers,storage engines and their internal mechanisms cannot author,amend,override or canonicalize law. AMENDMENT:only the governed complete successor procedure,with current permission,version,lineage,integrity and seal verification,changes the official Codex;storage technology never grants amendment authority.

AVAILABILITY:failure of unrelated data,index,network or runtime capabilities does not invalidate an independently verified local read path to the same current formal Codex. BASIS:governance adjudication requires the registered single official entry and current integrity,version,lineage,scope and seal evidence. FAILURE:if that authoritative read path is unavailable or unverified,dependent adjudication fails closed;no mirror,cache,legacy source or older generation becomes fallback authority. PROHIBITED-TOOLS:B166 and C81 remain controlling.

AUTHENTICITY:the formal Codex has one official entry and one current sealed generation;identity,version,content root,lineage and seal are verified deterministically,not elected or inferred from availability or storage technology. COPIES:non-authoritative consumer copies,mirrors,exports and legacy sources never become official by location,engine name or freshness. MIGRATION:only a complete independently verified governed successor with atomic official-entry activation and rollback may replace the physical store while preserving one logical authority;legacy evidence alone grants no production execution permission. FAILURE:missing or conflicting proof denies authoritative citation;B166 and C81 tool prohibitions remain controlling.

BOUNDARY:authorized downstream stores may consume Codex citations,derived status and audit results only;they cannot mutate the formal Codex. STORAGE-NO-POWER:database rows,engines,triggers,procedures and storage ownership confer no lawmaking or amendment authority. CHANGE:only the governed complete successor procedure may amend the official Codex with current permission,transaction,version,lineage,integrity and seal verification. HISTORY:sealed predecessor text remains immutable;this successor does not authorize in-place mutation of a sealed generation.

AVAILABILITY:unrelated structured-data,index,network or runtime failure must not interrupt an independently verified authorized local read path to the same current formal Codex. OFFICIAL-ENTRY:read-only access retains current version,scope,integrity,lineage and seal verification. FAILURE:absence of that verified formal read path blocks dependent adjudication;no projection,legacy source or older law is automatically promoted. BOUNDARY:B166 and C81 production tool prohibitions remain controlling;availability is never an exception permitting prohibited execution.

AUTHENTICITY:one registered official entry,one current sealed generation and deterministic identity,integrity,version,lineage and seal matching;storage engine choice confers no authenticity or amendment power. COPIES:mirrors,exports,caches and legacy sources are non-authoritative. SUCCESSOR:only independently verified complete governed migration may atomically activate a replacement physical store at the same logical official entry,with rollback and preserved lineage;this is not permission to run a prohibited production tool or legacy fallback. FAILURE:missing,stale or conflicting authority proof denies citation.

DEPENDENCIES:criticality is determined by the current certified required-capability contract,never by engine,service or tool name. CORE-CRITICAL:failure blocks the dependent core;CAPABILITY-CRITICAL:failure blocks only the dependent capability;OPTIONAL:failure reports bounded degradation without stopping unrelated work. ORDER:follow current B26 and B30 dependency,readiness,deadline and shutdown principles;no legacy fixed sequence controls current execution. PROHIBITED-TOOLS:B166 and C81 remain controlling;criticality or availability never permits a prohibited tool or unverified fallback.

FORMAL-TOOLS:only registered local-owned tool capabilities with a current owner,scope,permission and verified lifecycle may execute;concrete approved-tool inventory is a subordinate business declaration and cannot create authority. LANGUAGE:only the eight implementation languages permitted by B166;allocation remains owner-contract business detail. PROHIBITIONS:PostgreSQL production database execution,psql,Npgsql production SQL consumers and external production SQL tools,services or subprocesses remain prohibited under B166 and C81;Python remains prohibited. SUBSTITUTION:unregistered,unverified or prohibited tool substitution is forbidden.
